extra.resolution: Fall back to stdout or a generic message when stderr is empty

issues.notes: RunCliAsync returned 'Error: {stderr}' when ExitCode != 0. If stderr was empty the user saw 'Error: ' with no details. Fixed: falls back to stdout or a generic message when stderr is empty.
issues.priority_note: Low — edge case; most CLI failures do write to stderr.
issues.title: RunCliAsync shows empty error message when CLI writes failure to stdout

extra.file: PreviewImpactAsync hardcodes fsutil hardlink list which is Windows-only
extra.resolution: Document that this tool is Windows-only (acceptable because the app is WinUI 3)

issues.notes: PreviewImpactAsync shells out to fsutil hardlink list which only exists on Windows. This is acceptable because the entire WinUI 3 app targets Windows, but it is undocumented. Status: wontfix — not a bug in the current Windows-only context.
issues.priority_note: Info — not a bug in the current Windows-only context, just missing documentation.
issues.title: PreviewImpactAsync fsutil hardlink list is Windows-only and undocumented

extra.file: WorkflowConstants fields referenced as private undefined names in ToolExecutor and WorkflowsViewModel
extra.resolution: Extracted to Models/WorkflowConstants.cs; both classes now reference the shared class

issues.notes: ToolExecutor.cs and WorkflowsViewModel.cs both referenced private extension-set fields that did not exist in the other class. Fixed by extracting to a shared Models/WorkflowConstants.cs.
issues.priority_note: High — workflows would throw at runtime when referenced from the wrong class.
issues.title: WorkflowConstants fields referenced as private undefined names

extra.file: ResolveScanPathAsync did not pass CancellationToken to GetScanHistoryPageAsync
extra.resolution: Added ct parameter to GetScanHistoryPageAsync call

issues.notes: ResolveScanPathAsync called _scanner.GetScanHistoryPageAsync without passing the CancellationToken, so cancellation requests during path resolution were ignored.
issues.priority_note: Medium — cancellation silently ignored during path resolution.
issues.title: ResolveScanPathAsync did not propagate CancellationToken

extra.file: FormatBytes had a dead private copy; callers were inconsistent
extra.resolution: Removed private copy; all callers now use ByteFormatter.FormatBytes

issues.notes: ToolExecutor.cs contained a private FormatBytes(ulong) method that was never called. All call sites already used ByteFormatter.FormatBytes. Removed the orphan method.
issues.priority_note: Low — dead code removal.
issues.title: Dead private FormatBytes method in ToolExecutor

extra.file: BuildApiMessages silently dropped ALL ChatRole.Tool messages
extra.resolution: Now includes tool result messages with role=tool, content, and tool_call_id

issues.notes: BuildApiMessages filtered out ALL ChatRole.Tool messages (m.Role != ChatRole.Tool). After any tool call, the next API request had zero context of what the tool returned, breaking multi-turn agentic loops after step 1. Critical fix.
issues.priority_note: Critical — broke the entire agentic loop after the first tool call.
issues.title: BuildApiMessages silently dropped ALL ChatRole.Tool messages

extra.file: ParseToolArguments called .ToString() on JsonElement values in Dictionary<string, object>
extra.resolution: Detects nested JsonElement and re-serializes/deserializes to unwrap

issues.notes: ParseToolArguments returned raw Dictionary<string, object> containing nested JsonElement values. Calling .ToString() on those produced 'System.Text.Json.JsonElement', causing silent empty-argument tool calls.
issues.priority_note: High — tools ran with empty/garbage arguments.
issues.title: ParseToolArguments produced 'System.Text.Json.JsonElement' for nested JsonElement values

extra.file: WorkflowFindHiddenFilesAsync/WorkflowFindReadOnlyAsync did bitwise AND on file SIZE with FileAttributes
extra.resolution: Now uses File.GetAttributes(kvp.Key) to read real file attributes

issues.notes: WorkflowFindHiddenFilesAsync and WorkflowFindReadOnlyAsync did kvp.Value.Size & FileAttributes.Hidden (bitwise AND on file SIZE). ScannedFileEntry has no attributes field — these workflows always returned empty results.
issues.priority_note: Critical — workflows always returned empty results.
issues.title: WorkflowFindHiddenFiles/ReadOnly did bitwise AND on file SIZE instead of attributes

extra.file: SearchFilesAsync empty-result message was copy-paste from GetLargestFilesAsync
extra.resolution: Changed message to 'No files match the current filters in the target directory.'

issues.notes: SearchFilesAsync returned 'No large files found.' when files existed but no results matched the filters. Fixed to say 'No files match the current filters in the target directory.'
issues.priority_note: Medium — misleading UX.
issues.title: SearchFilesAsync error message was copy-paste from GetLargestFilesAsync

extra.file: GetString/GetOptionalString called .ToString() on JsonElement
extra.resolution: Explicit JsonElement unwrap: GetString() for string-typed, GetRawText() for others

issues.notes: GetString/GetOptionalString called v.ToString() without checking for JsonElement, which produces 'System.Text.Json.JsonElement' instead of the actual value.
issues.priority_note: Medium — produced garbage string values for JsonElement arguments.
issues.title: GetString/GetOptionalString produced 'System.Text.Json.JsonElement' for JsonElement values

extra.file: WorkflowFindLargeFilesAsync always did a fresh deep scan; ignored GetLargestFileEntriesAsync cache
extra.resolution: Now uses GetLargestFileEntriesAsync which reuses cached scan when available

issues.notes: WorkflowFindLargeFilesAsync called _scanner.ScanDirectoryAsync directly (always fresh deep scan). Fixed to use GetLargestFileEntriesAsync which checks the scan-history cache first.
issues.priority_note: Medium — wasted time and I/O on repeated calls.
issues.title: WorkflowFindLargeFilesAsync ignored GetLargestFileEntriesAsync cache

extra.file: PredictStorageAsync divided by zero when all timestamps are identical
extra.resolution: Guarded denominator with Math.Abs(denom) < 1e-9 check

issues.notes: PredictStorageAsync computed slope = (n*sumXY - sumX*sumY) / (n*sumX2 - sumX*sumX). When all scan timestamps are identical the denominator is zero, producing Infinity/NaN. Fixed with guard.
issues.priority_note: Medium — produced garbage prediction on repeated scans at the same timestamp.
issues.title: PredictStorageAsync zero-division when all timestamps are identical

extra.file: RunCliAsync timeout and user cancellation both returned the same generic message
extra.resolution: Check ct.IsCancellationRequested and return distinct messages

issues.notes: RunCliAsync returned 'Operation timed out.' for both actual timeouts and user cancellation, misleading users about what happened.
issues.priority_note: Medium — poor UX for cancelled operations.
issues.title: RunCliAsync returned same message for timeout and user cancellation

extra.file: analyze_file_patterns tool was in ExecuteAsync switch but not in GetToolDefinitions
extra.resolution: Added tool definition with path parameter

issues.notes: analyze_file_patterns was implemented in ToolExecutor.ExecuteAsync but was not exposed in AIAssistantViewModel.GetToolDefinitions(), so the model could never call it.
issues.priority_note: High — tool was completely unreachable by the model.
issues.title: analyze_file_patterns tool unreachable — missing from GetToolDefinitions

extra.file: MaxToolIterations exhaustion was silent — no message added to chat
extra.resolution: Added explicit message when loop exhausts

issues.notes: When MaxToolIterations (10) was exhausted, the agentic loop exited silently with no message shown to the user. Fixed by adding an explicit message explaining the limit was reached.
issues.priority_note: Medium — user had no feedback that the loop stopped.
issues.title: MaxToolIterations exhaustion was silent

extra.file: ToolExecutor.Dispose() did not dispose owned ScannerService
extra.resolution: Added _scanner?.Dispose() to Dispose method

issues.notes: ToolExecutor owns a ScannerService but Dispose() was a no-op. The scanner subprocess handle was never released until GC finalization.
issues.priority_note: Medium — resource leak on repeated open/close of AI assistant.
issues.title: ToolExecutor.Dispose did not dispose owned ScannerService

extra.file: ToolCallResponse missing Id property — tool_call_id mismatch with Ollama
extra.resolution: Added Id property to ToolCallResponse and use Ollama-returned tool_call id instead of generating a new Guid

issues.notes: Ollama API returns tool_calls with an id field (e.g. call_abc123), but C# ToolCallResponse has no Id property to capture it. AIAssistantViewModel generates a new random Guid (call_{Guid.NewGuid():N}) instead of using Ollama id. This means tool_call_id in tool result messages does not match the id in the assistant tool_calls, violating the OpenAI-compatible tool-use spec. The Rust GUI correctly preserves call.id.
issues.priority_note: High — violates Ollama/OpenAI tool-use contract; some models may reject mismatched ids.
issues.title: ToolCallResponse drops Ollama tool_call id — tool_call_id mismatch in multi-turn loops

extra.file: Assistant tool_calls not persisted in _messages for multi-turn context
extra.resolution: AddMessage now persists assistant tool_calls messages to _messages so BuildApiMessages includes them on follow-up turns

issues.notes: When the model returns tool_calls, the assistant message is added to apiMessages but NOT to _messages. On a follow-up user turn, BuildApiMessages() rebuilds from _messages, losing the previous assistant tool_calls. The resulting API context is [system, user, tool_results, final_assistant] instead of [system, user, assistant(tool_calls), tool_results, final_assistant]. The Rust GUI correctly persists assistant messages with tool_calls in conversation_history.
issues.priority_note: Medium — breaks strict OpenAI tool-use message ordering; may confuse models on follow-up turns.
issues.title: Assistant tool_calls lost between turns — not persisted in _messages

extra.file: GetInt throws InvalidOperationException on JsonElement numbers larger than int.MaxValue
extra.resolution: GetInt uses TryGetInt64 with Math.Clamp fallback instead of GetInt32, avoiding InvalidOperationException on large numbers

issues.notes: GetInt calls je.GetInt32() when the JsonElement is a number. If the model sends a value larger than int.MaxValue (e.g. min_size_mb=999999), GetInt32 throws InvalidOperationException. The fallback int.TryParse(je.GetRawText(), ...) also fails for large numbers, silently returning defaultValue. This affects any tool parameter that could receive large integer values from the model.
issues.priority_note: Low — only affects edge cases with very large integer parameters.
issues.title: GetInt overflows on JsonElement numbers larger than int.MaxValue

extra.file: ExtractDirectoryPath does not handle UNC paths
extra.resolution: ExtractDirectoryPath now matches UNC share anchors (\\server\share) with the same candidate-growth logic as drive-letter paths

issues.notes: ExtractDirectoryPath only handles drive-letter anchored paths (C:\...) and quoted/backticked paths. UNC paths like \\server\share are not matched by the drive-letter regex and fall through to null. Users targeting network shares get no path resolution.
issues.priority_note: Low — only affects users with network share paths.
issues.title: ExtractDirectoryPath does not resolve UNC network share paths

extra.file: ResolveToolChoice greeting detection misses hi without trailing space
extra.resolution: Replaced lower.Contains("hi ") with a word-boundary regex match (\bhi\b) via IsGreeting helper

issues.notes: lower.Contains('hi ') only matches when hi is followed by a space. If the user types hi at the end of a message (e.g. 'Just saying hi') or 'hi!' with punctuation, it is not matched and the tool choice may be forced to required instead of auto.
issues.priority_note: Low — cosmetic; affects only short greeting messages.
issues.title: ResolveToolChoice greeting detection misses hi without trailing space

extra.file: BuildApiMessages includes ToolCallId on non-tool messages
extra.resolution: BuildApiMessages no longer sets ToolCallId on User/Assistant messages; added WhenWritingNull to JsonOptions to omit null fields

issues.notes: BuildApiMessages sets ToolCallId = msg.ToolCallId for User and Assistant messages as well as Tool messages. For non-tool messages the property is typically null, but including it in the payload is semantically incorrect and could confuse downstream API consumers.
issues.priority_note: Low — cosmetic; property is null for non-tool messages so no runtime impact.
issues.title: BuildApiMessages sets ToolCallId on User/Assistant messages unnecessarily
